scope: Typed task ownership, deliberately cancellation-insensitive gates, supervisor joins, late outer result refusal and original close-failure retry. C separately owns API/constructor and complete component-graph review.

newMethods.name: testBusyRefusalKeepsTheRegisteredOperationAndReleasesItsSlotAtTerminal
newMethods.meaning: The first gated operation remains registered while a second is refused with .busy; its body stays unentered and a later new operation obtains the released slot after actual completion.

newMethods.name: testExternalInvalidationCancelsAndWaitsForTheLateOuterDestinationResult
newMethods.meaning: Cancellation and synthetic native close are observed while the intentionally insensitive outer result remains gated. Both operation and invalidation remain unfinished; after release the late value is refused with .inactive and invalidation drains.

newMethods.name: testNativeCloseFailureStillJoinsTheOuterResultAndRetriesTheSameOwnedGrant
newMethods.meaning: One injected original close failure remains visible while the outer operation is gated. Invalidation joins the late result before surfacing .sessionCloseFailed; explicit retry closes the identical grant without a new create or validation.

newMethods.name: testSourceBindingRefusalClosesTheOriginalGrantWithoutJoiningItsAwaitingProducer
newMethods.meaning: A successfully constructed synthetic binding intentionally lacks the source head census; original source refusal must close the grant and return through the awaiting producer without a join cycle.

ownershipAndCleanup: Gate waiters are registered/resumed under a lock. Cancellation alone does not open a gate or mark an observed task complete.
Each ProducerLifetimeTask retains the actual typed Task<Value,Error>; the finished marker is opened in its exit defer, and value/result is still awaited to join.
The registry retains cancellation, observation and join closures for every observed task. Test-body tasks do not create new registry entries after the supervisor seals it.

The detached cleanup supervisor does not inherit the XCTest caller's cancellation. It releases all control gates, requests cancellation, registers the producer/source release task and then seals the registry.
Fixture removal follows completion observation, explicit result joins for all entries, successful release and source.state == .idle.
If cleanup observation or release fails, the test records failure and deliberately aborts instead of deleting a fixture with unresolved ownership.
Probe event/counter state is locked; the injected close failure is observed before cleanup may clear only the remaining injection. The test result is retained and rethrown after successful cleanup.
requiredRunnerPolicy: The eventual component runner must set core dump size to zero.
A cleanup fatalError is a process/cohort failure with retained fixture evidence. It must never be reported as successful cleanup or credit for methods that did not complete.
The external finite test-process deadline/group ownership remains required; these source helpers are not a replacement for that controller.
scopeLimits: All session/capture/native probe responses and filesystem fixture names are synthetic; no existing account or original capture is read.

The tests target internal withOwnedOperation/invalidate and the original source-owner refusal. They do not invoke execute/produce, manufacture AnyHeartNativeMigrationCompletion, call the actual migration executor or qualify destination authority.
The late-result control models the outer operation boundary; it is not an actual App/UI/session integration test.
No Swift parser/compiler, test, filesystem fixture, native runtime or Oracle command was executed for this peer.
